sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Columbia County, FL?
sections.html:
Three offices share the job. The Columbia County Property Appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, local taxing authorities adopt budgets and millage, and the Columbia County Tax Collector issues bills and takes payment from its Lake City offices.

The tax collector's main line is 386-758-1077 and the Tax Department answers at 386-758-1080. Exemption and value questions go to the Property Appraiser at (386) 758-1083. The Clerk of Court, at 386-719-7580 for tax deed questions, runs the deed sales that follow long delinquency.

sections.h2: When is Columbia County property tax due?
sections.html:
The regular annual bill is due by March 31, and unpaid taxes generally become delinquent April 1. Bills go out in November, and the early-payment discount starts at 4% that month and falls one point each month through February.

A TRIM notice in August is a proposal, not the payment bill. The tax collector says a proposed-tax notice differs from the annual bill, so check it for values, exemptions and hearing dates. Florida law gives next-working-day treatment when a deadline lands on a weekend or legal holiday for qualifying payments, but call the office if the date is close.

sections.h2: What payment options does the Columbia County tax collector offer?
sections.html:
You can pay online or by phone, in person, by mail or at the Lake City drive-through and drop box. The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum and a $1.50 e-check fee for online or phone payments, and says it receives no part of the card fee.

  • Search by owner name, address or account number in the property tax portal.
  • Mortgage escrow customers should confirm the lender paid the right year, to avoid a duplicate payment.
  • E-billing is available, registered one property account at a time.
  • A duplicate notice can go to a second recipient, but the owner remains responsible.

sections.h2: How do the quarterly installments work in Columbia County?
sections.html:
The installment plan lets an owner prepay the current year in four payments if estimated tax is over $100 per notice. Submit Form DR-534 to the tax collector by April 30. The first payment confirms participation.

The first two installments use prior-year tax as the estimate, and later ones adjust to actual tax. A late first installment is accepted through July 31 without the June discount. The plan does not cover delinquent taxes.

sections.h2: Can I make partial payments on Columbia County property tax?
sections.html:
Yes, on current taxes from November 1 through March 31, by signing a partial-payment agreement with the office. No early-payment discounts apply to partial payments, and the full balance must be paid by March 31.

Tracking is the owner's job, and the published local plan mails no balance reminder before April 1. Any unpaid balance becomes delinquent with interest and costs, and partial payments do not stop a certificate sale if real estate tax remains unpaid. State law leaves partial payments to the tax collector's discretion before delinquency.

sections.h2: What homestead and tax relief programs apply in Columbia County?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser decides homestead, disability, widow or widower, veteran, senior and agricultural benefits. The usual filing deadline is March 1, and the Florida homestead exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school tax as well.

Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and a sale resets the property to just value the next January 1. Disabled ex-servicemembers get a $5,000 reduction in assessed value, and veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability can get a discount equal to the VA disability percentage. Homestead tax deferral applications go to the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

The tax collector's page also mentions income-based help and certain vacancy reductions for service assessments. Call to confirm which one fits.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Columbia County tax when a house is sold?
sections.html:
The closing agent settles current-year tax from the seller's proceeds, and the tax collector confirms payment status. Ask for an exact payoff for your closing date, since interest and costs change the amount.

A tax certificate is a lien and does not transfer ownership. Under section 197.502 a certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the issue year, and the Clerk of Court holds the sale. Redemption is available until a tax deed is issued, unless the buyer has paid the clerk in full, so call the Tax Department at 386-758-1080 with your parcel number before any sale date. The office accepts cash, money order, cashier's check or card for certificate redemption and cautions against assuming a personal check works.

sections.h2: What if I disagree with my Columbia County value?
sections.html:
Contact the Property Appraiser first, then use the Value Adjustment Board if needed. A value petition goes to the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and an exemption denial can be appealed within 30 days after the denial letter is mailed.

Payment questions and value disputes belong to different offices, and a petition does not replace paying the bill the tax collector sends in November.

faqs.q: When is Columbia County property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: Regular annual taxes are due by March 31 and generally become delinquent April 1. Discounts run from 4% in November to 1% in February.

faqs.q: How do I join the Columbia County installment plan?
faqs.a: Submit Form DR-534 to the tax collector by April 30, and estimated taxes must exceed $100 per notice. Your first payment confirms participation.

faqs.q: What card fee does the Columbia County tax collector charge?
faqs.a: The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum, plus a $1.50 e-check fee, for online or phone payments.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Columbia County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Call the Property Appraiser at (386) 758-1083. The usual filing deadline is March 1.

faqs.q: Who runs tax deed sales in Columbia County?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Court conducts them and issues deeds to winning bidders. Tax deed questions go to 386-719-7580.
